responsibility.value: Marker contract exposing `int MusicStoreId` that identifies an entity as belonging to a single store/tenant. Implementing this interface is what makes an entity subject to automatic tenant-scoped query filtering.

Owns: The MusicStoreId contract itself — nothing else; this is a pure marker/data interface
doesNotOwn: Enforcement — this interface does nothing on its own; enforcement is entirely in eNote.Infrastructure.Data.ENoteContext.OnModelCreating

collaborators.detail: OnModelCreating reflects over modelBuilder.Model.GetEntityTypes(), finds every CLR type assignable to ITenantScoped, and generically invokes SetTenantFilter<TEntity> to apply `HasQueryFilter(e => GetStoreId() == null || e.MusicStoreId == GetStoreId())`

contracts: Any entity implementing this interface is automatically enrolled in the store-scoping global query filter — no per-entity opt-in code is needed beyond implementing the interface.
GetStoreId() returning null (caller has no store context, e.g. an admin or a student) disables the filter for that request — the query is unscoped in that case, by design.
assumptions: Adding ITenantScoped to a new entity is sufficient and necessary for that entity to be tenant-isolated. If a developer forgets to implement it on a new store-owned entity, that entity gets NO automatic tenant filter and is a silent data-isolation gap — the reflection loop only catches types that explicitly declare the interface.

InstrumentRental separately gets an explicit `HasQueryFilter` at OnModelCreating line 41 (combining IsActive + store scoping) in addition to whatever the generic ITenantScoped loop would apply — EF Core's HasQueryFilter is last-write-wins per entity type, so the explicit call after the generic loop is what actually takes effect for InstrumentRental. This ordering is load-bearing: if the generic loop were ever reordered to run after the explicit calls, or if the explicit call were modified without preserving the store-scoping clause, tenant isolation for that entity type would silently regress.
invariants: GetStoreId() resolves via ICurrentActor and is memoized per ENoteContext instance (`_storeId` field) — consistent within one request/DbContext lifetime.
failureModes: Missing interface implementation on a new tenant-owned entity — no exception, just an unscoped entity (silent cross-tenant read risk).
A future explicit HasQueryFilter added after the generic loop, without an `&& MusicStoreId == GetStoreId()` clause, silently overrides and removes tenant scoping for that entity type.
architecturalNotes: This is the actual mechanism behind the tenant-isolation guarantee referenced by the project's recent 'Fix tenant isolation filter' work — the interface itself is trivial, but it's the single point of truth for which entities get scoped. Any semantic review of tenant isolation should center on ENoteContext.OnModelCreating, not this interface file.
